technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD 1.1.0 build, module metadata, documentation conventions, and performance-testing utilities rather than introducing a new documentation or benchmarking framework.
Treat the module descriptions for developers and end users as one maintained documentation set, generated or linked from module-definition Javadocs where practical.
Publish RPMs through the existing Maven-compatible spring.io repository layout under the specified 1.1.0.RELEASE coordinates.
Use repeatable benchmark scripts and record broker, producer, consumer, machine, message-size, throughput, and latency settings with every benchmark result.
Use EC2 instances with dedicated broker and client roles for Kafka testing, and document the infrastructure as reproducible configuration rather than provisioning a new permanent environment.
Use Kafka's in-built performance producer and consumer utilities for the Kafka baseline tests and the existing Rabbit performance test tooling for Rabbit benchmarks.
Document message-header compatibility changes in the troubleshooting documentation, including symptoms, affected 1.0 batch jobs, and remediation guidance.
Target the existing Spring XD release branch and its compatible Java and dependency versions; do not perform an unrelated framework or Java-version migration.
assumptions: The existing source repository, build system, module definitions, RPM packaging scripts, and performance-test utilities are available and buildable with limited repair.
Credentials and permissions for the spring.io repository and the required EC2 account are available before implementation begins.
The requested work is documentation, configuration, benchmarking, packaging, and release enablement; it does not require new production messaging features.
A representative Rabbit environment and Kafka environment can be provisioned using existing infrastructure or short-lived test resources.
The Kafka engineering-team baseline is used as a reference target; exact reproduction is not guaranteed because hardware, network, Kafka version, and cloud performance may differ.
The module documentation scope includes all modules present in the target Spring XD release, with approximately 15 to 25 modules.
Benchmark execution includes a reasonable number of repeat runs and basic result validation, but not a prolonged multi-week performance campaign.
Work-hour estimates include implementation, local verification, and review by the developer performing the work, but exclude waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure availability.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the release branch, identify affected modules and existing documentation, benchmark, packaging, and deployment assets, verify the build, and create the implementation checklist.

Review each Spring XD module definition and implementation, draft concise purpose and capability descriptions for developers and users, and place the content in the project documentation or module Javadocs according to existing conventions.

activities.activity_name: Module documentation validation and publication preparation
activities.activity_description: Build the Javadocs or documentation site, check links and formatting, verify that all modules are covered, and prepare the final documentation changes for review.

activities.activity_name: RPM packaging and spring.io repository publication
activities.activity_description: Inspect and, where necessary, update RPM packaging and release metadata, build the 1.1.0.RELEASE RPM artifacts, validate installation metadata and checksums, and publish the artifacts to the specified spring.io repository location.

activities.activity_name: Rabbit benchmark planning and environment setup
activities.activity_description: Define Rabbit benchmark scenarios and metrics, inspect the existing performance utilities, configure the broker and client environment, and create repeatable commands or scripts for the test runs.

Run the Rabbit performance tests across representative configurations, capture throughput and latency results, investigate anomalous runs, summarize findings, and produce reference guidance for XD cluster setup.

Research suitable EC2 instance types, storage, networking, availability-zone placement, operating-system requirements, broker/client topology, and estimated resource needs for Kafka performance testing.
Identify and document Kafka broker, topic, partition, replication, producer, consumer, JVM, operating-system, and network configurations needed for repeatable performance tests.

activities.activity_name: Kafka benchmark harness and environment implementation
activities.activity_description: Provision or configure the test environment, install the required Kafka version and dependencies, prepare the in-built producer and consumer utilities, create test scripts, and verify end-to-end execution.

activities.activity_name: Kafka baseline benchmark execution and analysis
activities.activity_description: Run controlled Kafka benchmark scenarios, repeat measurements, collect throughput and latency data, compare results with the referenced engineering baseline, diagnose major deviations, and document reproducible results and limitations.

activities.activity_name: Message-header compatibility investigation and troubleshooting documentation
activities.activity_description: Compare 1.0 and 1.1 message-header behavior, identify serialization or deserialization compatibility issues affecting reused batch jobs, reproduce representative failures where possible, and add troubleshooting guidance to the project wiki or equivalent documentation.

activities.activity_name: Integrated verification, review, and delivery cleanup
activities.activity_description: Review all code, configuration, benchmark scripts, documentation, and release artifacts; run targeted regression checks; correct defects; verify links and artifact availability; and prepare the final change set.
